title: How immune defenses recognize and respond
intro: The immune system is a network of barriers, cells, organs and proteins, not a single strength setting. It must respond to threats while limiting injury to the body. More inflammation is not automatically better protection.

sections.heading: First defenses
paragraphs: Skin and mucous membranes limit entry. Innate defenses respond quickly through cells and chemical signals; inflammation recruits help but can also cause swelling and discomfort.

sections.heading: Targeted responses
paragraphs: B and T lymphocytes recognize particular targets. Antibodies can bind targets, while different T cells coordinate responses or attack infected cells. These roles work together rather than compete.

sections.heading: Memory
paragraphs: After some exposures, memory cells support a faster later response. Vaccines build useful protection without requiring the full disease, but protection varies and is not a guarantee against every infection.

sections.heading: When regulation fails
paragraphs: Allergy responds to usually harmless substances; autoimmunity targets the body. Immunodeficiency reduces particular defenses. These are different problems, so a generic immune-boosting supplement is not a universal treatment.

sections.heading: Practical care
paragraphs: Follow recommended vaccination and hygiene advice, especially with immune-suppressing treatment. Recurrent unusual infections deserve review. Serious illness or fever during certain treatments requires the team's urgent plan, not waiting for supplements.

A diagram explains typical structure, not the cause of an individual symptom. Before a consultation, note when a change began, what brings it on and how it affects daily activities. Bring previous results and ask how the findings fit together.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira asks whether more inflammation means stronger immunity. Her clinician explains that controlling an overactive response can protect tissue.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben checks his vaccination plan before immune-suppressing treatment rather than choosing a supplement advertised as a universal boost.
